title: Monolayer van der Waals kagome lattice for high-temperature flat-band physics
authors: Hyungkun Bong, Choongjae Won, Seongyong Lee, Soomin Oh, Phuong X. Nguyen, Raghav Chaturvedi, Sehyun Oh, Jiyong Han, Paul Malinowski, Chad Mowers, Jimin Kim, Sae Hee Ryu, Hyunjong Lee, Jinhyeok Choi, Sangsu Yer, Chris Jozwiak, Aaron Bostwick, Eli Rotenberg, Craig M. Polley, Matthew D. Watson, Timur K. Kim, Heejun Yang, Jieun Lee, Kin Fai Mak, Jie Shan, Jae-Hoon Park, Gil Young Cho, Kyle M. Shen, Mingu Kang
abstract: Kagome lattice materials host a remarkably rich landscape of novel quantum phenomena, all arising from the intrinsic interplay of topology, correlation, and frustration. While previous studies have been mostly limited to bulk three-dimensional (3D) kagome crystals, the realization of a true two-dimensional (2D) kagome system has remained a long-standing goal, to unlock fundamentally new physics and engineering pathways inaccessible in 3D systems. In this work, we establish the first ideal 2D monolayer kagome lattices by leveraging a novel and versatile van der Waals (vdW) kagome family, A2T3X4 (A = K, Rb, Cs; T = Ni, Pd, Pt; X = S, Se). Our nano-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (nano-ARPES) directly characterizes the electronic structure of A2T3X4 down to the monolayer limit, notably revealing an isolated kagome-derived flat band just below the Fermi level. Via gate-engineering of 2D A2T3X4, the kagome flat band can be further tuned to the Fermi level, allowing direct access to the partially filled flat band physics and establishing a qualitatively new 2D flat band platform. Compared to existing moire-based artificial flat band systems, this vdW kagome-based intrinsic flat band system realizes more than 220 times higher flat band electron density, opening an entirely new density and energy regime for exploring 2D flat band physics. Harnessing this high-electron-density flat band in 2D vdW kagome system provides a clear pathway to scale emergent flat band phenomena - such as fractional quantum anomalous Hall states - to far higher temperatures than currently achievable, as long-envisioned in theory and further supported by our many-body calculations.
summary: This work introduces the $	ext{A}_2	ext{T}_3	ext{X}_4$ van der Waals family as the first ideal 2D material for studying kagome physics. By combining nano-ARPES and theory, the authors confirm the existence of a highly dense, intrinsic flat band. This platform promises to enable the study of correlated topological states, such as the FQAH state, at significantly higher temperatures than previously achieved.
main_problem: The primary goal is to establish and study ideal two-dimensional (2D) kagome lattices to unlock novel quantum phenomena inaccessible in bulk 3D systems.
main_result: The $	ext{A}_2	ext{T}_3	ext{X}_4$ vdW family provides the first ideal 2D platform, exhibiting an intrinsic, highly dense flat band that can host high-temperature correlated states like the FQAH state.
method: The work combines experimental characterization using nano-ARPES with theoretical predictions from DFT and many-body calculations.
model_or_system: The system is the van der Waals (vdW) kagome lattice $	ext{A}_2	ext{T}_3	ext{X}_4$, which is synthesized and exfoliated into a true 2D monolayer limit. This structure is compared to Moiré systems and modeled using tight-binding Hamiltonians.
key_observables: Isolated kagome-derived flat band, fractional quantum anomalous Hall state (FQAH) gap ($\approx 14–29 	ext{ meV}$), and high flat band electron density ($	ext{n} \approx 1.0 	ext{ nm}^{-2}$).
important_parameters: The flat band electron density is $>220$ times higher than Moiré systems, and the physics is predicted to be stable at higher temperatures.
main_assumptions: The vdW nature allows for clean exfoliation and the electronic structure is assumed to be dominated by the $d_{xy}$ orbitals forming the kagome network.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the ideal 2D kagome dispersion, show optical images of exfoliated flakes, and present ARPES spectra confirming the flat band and Dirac points, alongside theoretical calculations of many-body spectra and Chern band analysis.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for 2D kagome systems, to identifying the $	ext{A}_2	ext{T}_3	ext{X}_4$ material family, characterizing the intrinsic flat band via ARPES, and finally using many-body theory to predict and confirm the existence of high-temperature correlated states like the FQAH state.
why_interesting: The realization of a high-density, intrinsic 2D flat band platform fundamentally changes the landscape for studying correlated topological states, offering a superior alternative to current Moiré-based systems for high-temperature physics.
